primary_source.title: 50 years of first passage percolation
primary_source.locators: Questions 13 and 15, printed page 37 / zero-based PDF page 36; context printed pages 34-35
primary_source.question_13_paraphrase: For every d>=2 and suitable edge distributions F, prove chi<1/2; in d=2 identify chi=1/3.
primary_source.question_15_paraphrase: Establish a positive fluctuation exponent in appropriate dimensions.
primary_source.formalization_limit: The source does not fix that distribution class or a unique meaning of variance scaling; context discusses several alternatives and the absence of flat edges.

working_convention_only: For an audit of variance powers, fix one law and one direction before n tends to infinity, and state explicitly whether chi is a log-variance limit or a liminf/limsup. No existence is assumed from the title.

supporting_primary_sources.checked_scope: Ordinary iid nonnegative lattice FPP, d>=2, atom at zero below bond-percolation criticality; exponential moments give concentration at sqrt(n/log n). Uniform[1,1+epsilon] meets those distribution assumptions.
The KPZ relation is conditional on matching upper and lower exponent definitions, with nearly-gamma and moment assumptions in this theorem; it does not determine the exponent values.
Polynomial improvement concerns a class of rotationally invariant Riemannian FPP, not the general lattice question.
